The Émile Boutmy scholarship is Sciences Po's principal funding scheme for students from outside the European Union, named after the university's founder. It takes the form of a reduction of tuition fees — either a total exemption or an exemption of €9,500 — and can be combined with other grants such as the Eiffel scholarship or French regional grants.

Programme Highlights

  • Tuition exemption of €9,500 per year — or a total exemption from tuition fees
  • Open to first-time, non-EU applicants to Sciences Po Bachelor's and Master's programmes
  • Can be combined with the Eiffel scholarship, CROUS and regional grants for living costs
  • Awarded on academic excellence, the admissions file and the candidate's background and goals

Who Should Apply

First-time applicants from outside the European Union who have been admitted (or are applying) to a Sciences Po Bachelor's or Master's programme. There is no separate nationality shortlist — every non-EU admitted student is automatically considered once the scholarship form is submitted on time.

Funding and Costs

The scholarship reduces tuition only: it pays no monthly living stipend, so budget for Paris living costs (typically €1,200–€1,600/month with university housing) and look at the Eiffel scholarship or French regional grants for maintenance support.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply for admission to your Sciences Po programme first, then complete the scholarship section of the application file by the deadline for your level. Key deadline information: Master's: 29 November 2026; undergraduate (foreign secondary schools): 13 January 2027; undergraduate (French secondary schools): 1 April 2027.

About Sciences Po

Sciences Po (Paris Institute of Political Studies) is one of Europe's leading universities for politics, international relations, law, economics and social sciences. The Émile Boutmy scholarship is its principal funding scheme for students from outside the European Union.

Official website: https://www.sciencespo.fr

Contact

Questions about this scholarship, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official scholarship page (see the Official Link section above). Always include your applicant ID or programme name so the admissions or scholarship team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements and deadlines on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form — transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
  • Deadlines shown in local time (CET/CEST) as published by the provider; convert to your own time zone before planning.
